description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v5.11.0: a place to write the rule that protects an account or a role, API keys that need no restart, and an audit that covers Identity's own messages. MyIdentityUserService gains the hook OnBeforeManageUserAsync(MyIdentityUserOperation, user), which runs after the caller gate and the operation's own checks, immediately before the first write of the administrative operations of IMyIdentityUserService on another user's account that the enum names (it numbers them 1 to 16 and names the direction of enable/disable and lock/unlock; it grows, so give a switch over it a default arm); Identity's validators, and the lockout and current-password checks of a change of another user's password, run after it, and SetTenantAdminAsync does not pass it the TenantAdmins it demotes. ResetPasswordAsync and ConfirmEmailManuallyAsync now refuse an account an API key is bound to (AccountBoundToApiKey) instead of writing the credential and silently switching the key off. IMyIdentityApiKeySource, which you implement, serves the keys an application stores itself: it is read once when the host starts, before the first request, by a hosted service that AddMyIdentity adds, in StartingAsync, before the StartAsync of every hosted service (migrate a table it reads before Run), and its entries are validated with the rules of configuration. IMyIdentityApiKeyService adds and removes keys with the host running, behind the gate of the administration of another user's account, with typed refusals; persisting is yours, and an add or a removal reaches only the instance that served it. MyIdentity:Authentication:ApiKeys:Enabled no longer needs a key in configuration when a source is registered, and that startup rule is now a validator that ValidateConfiguration() does not report. MyIdentityRoleService and MyIdentityPermissionAdminService gain the hook OnBeforeManageRoleAsync(MyIdentityRoleOperationContext) (create, rename and delete a tenant role; save a matrix, remove a row, upsert; add, change and remove a user-role assignment), with the same rule of where it runs; removing or changing an assignment reads one more row. MyIdentityMessageDescriberAudit.FindUntranslated also audits a subclass of IdentityErrorDescriber (it used to throw ArgumentException for one) and now lists fourteen new describer messages until you override them; the package still ships no text in another language. Documentation (MI-54): the per-user DPAPI default (KeyProtection Auto without a thumbprint, and DpapiCurrentUser) needs the user profile loaded, which under IIS is the application pool's Load User Profile option set to true, or use DpapiLocalMachine or a certificate; startup does not check it, so it may fail on first use. Fixed before the release (5.10.0 has both defects): IssueJwtAsync refuses a locked-out account before it verifies the password, so wrong passwords no longer replace an administrator's lock by a 30-minute lockout (the answer is still InvalidCredentials), and the password-reset link goes to the address stored on the account, not to the one typed. A refusal across tenants no longer tells the target's role: the user administration's gate and a TenantAdmin's role assignments answer as for an account outside the tenant (one case moves from RoleNotFound to PermissionDenied). No schema change, nothing removed or changed in the public surface, nothing added to an existing interface. Dependencies: the six packages of the nuspec move from 10.0.14 to 10.0.15 (a project that references one of them directly below 10.0.15 gets NU1605 until it moves it), and the System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs pin stays, although the restore no longer needs it. The package validation baseline is 5.10.0. Upgrading from 5.10.0: MyIdentity/UPGRADE.md §55.
title: Kerberos.MyIdentity
